h: Fish, forts and a fresh sea breeze
p: Southsea is a cracking spot for an aquarium, because the minute you step back outside you've got a proper seaside promenade to play with. Blue Reef faces straight out over the Solent on Clarence Esplanade, so you can watch the ferries, hovercraft and big ships sliding past before you even go in. Kids who've just been staring at fish through glass tend to get a second wind when they spot something huge heading for the harbour.

Inside, the trick is to slow right down. Pick a tank and stay with it for a few minutes rather than marching past every window. The shy ones come out once you stop moving, and little ones love being the first to spot a hidden fish in the rocks. If anyone's nervous in dim, busy spaces, quieter times such as weekday mornings outside the school holidays are usually calmer.

Make the rest of the afternoon count. Southsea Castle, built for Henry VIII, sits along the front, Southsea Common gives you acres of grass for a run-about or a picnic, and Clarence Pier has the classic seaside amusements and rides for anyone who isn't ready to go home yet. It's all flat, easy walking along the prom, which makes it a good fit for buggies and grandparents too.
From Hayling, it's a straightforward drive back across the bridge and along to Portsmouth, so you can be home for tea with a bag full of stories about sharks and starfish.
